title: 4.1 Asexual Reproduction
description: Types and examples of asexual reproduction including fission, fragmentation, budding, and vegetative propagation

questions.question: Which of the following best distinguishes living things from non-living matter?
questions.explanation: Reproduction is one of the unique characteristics of life that best distinguishes living things from non-living matter.

questions.question: How many parents are involved in asexual reproduction?
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction involves only one parent and produces genetically identical offspring.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about asexual reproduction?
options: It produces identical copies of the parent
questions.correctAnswer: It produces identical copies of the parent
questions.explanation: In asexual reproduction, each organism is capable of producing identical copies of itself without gametes.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of asexual reproduction?
options: Greater ability to adapt to changing environments
Offspring are genetically different from the parent
questions.explanation: Advantages include no mate needed, no gametes needed, and all good characteristics are passed on to offspring.

questions.question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of asexual reproduction?
options: Offspring take too long to develop
questions.explanation: Little variation is created, making adaptation to changing environments unlikely.

questions.question: In binary fission, the parent organism divides into how many equal parts?
questions.explanation: In binary fission, the organism divides into two approximately equal parts, each growing into an individual similar to the parent.

questions.question: Binary fission is common among which of the following groups?
questions.explanation: Binary fission is common among bacteria, algae, and protozoa.

questions.question: Before a bacterium divides in binary fission, what must happen to its nucleus?
options: It is replicated to produce two identical copies
questions.correctAnswer: It is replicated to produce two identical copies
questions.explanation: The bacterial nucleus is replicated to produce two identical copies so each daughter cell receives one copy.

questions.question: Multiple fission is common in which of the following organisms?
questions.explanation: In multiple fission, the nucleus divides repeatedly, producing many daughter cells, which is common in malarial parasites.

questions.question: In fragmentation, what happens to the parent organism?
options: It divides into two equal parts
It breaks into parts that develop into whole organisms
questions.correctAnswer: It breaks into parts that develop into whole organisms
questions.explanation: Fragmentation involves the breakdown of a parent organism into parts that each develop into a whole organism.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms reproduces by fragmentation?
questions.explanation: Spirogyra, a filamentous green alga, undergoes fragmentation resulting in many filaments.

questions.question: In budding, the two daughter cells produced are typically:
questions.explanation: In budding, the organism divides into two unequal parts; a bulge forms on the side of the cell.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms reproduces by budding?
questions.explanation: In yeast, a bud develops on the surface of the cell; the nucleus divides and one daughter nucleus migrates into the bud.

questions.question: Which invertebrate animal is known to reproduce by budding?
questions.explanation: Budding occurs commonly in some invertebrate animals such as hydra.

questions.question: Vegetative propagation is a method of asexual reproduction in:
questions.explanation: Vegetative propagation is a method of asexual reproduction in plants where structures like roots, stems, and buds give rise to new individuals.

questions.question: Runners in plants such as strawberry are also known as:
questions.explanation: Runners (stolons) originate from an auxiliary bud and grow along the soil surface, producing new plants at nodes.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a modified stem that stores starch?
questions.explanation: Tubers are modified stems that store starch, as seen in potatoes.

questions.question: Which of the following underground structures functions as a storage unit and has enlarged fleshy leaves?
questions.explanation: A bulb is a modified stem with enlarged fleshy leaves emerging from the stem, functioning as an underground storage unit.

questions.question: Corms are similar to rhizomes but differ because they are:
questions.explanation: Corms are similar to rhizomes but are more rounded and fleshy, like in gladiolus.

questions.question: In artificial grafting, the stem portion of the plant that is grafted is called the:
questions.explanation: The stem of the plant to be grafted is known as the scion, while the root portion is called the stock.

questions.question: In artificial vegetative propagation, which method involves bending a stem and covering it with soil while still attached to the parent?
questions.explanation: Layering involves bending a stem attached to the plant and covering it with soil to produce roots.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of artificial vegetative propagation?
questions.explanation: Cutting is an artificial method where a stem portion with nodes is placed in moist soil to root, as in hibiscus.

questions.question: Parthenogenesis is a form of asexual reproduction in which:
options: An unfertilized egg develops into an adult
A fertilized egg develops into an adult
A bud detaches from the parent
questions.correctAnswer: An unfertilized egg develops into an adult
questions.explanation: Parthenogenesis is a form of asexual reproduction in which an unfertilized egg develops into an adult organism.

questions.question: In honeybees, bees produced through parthenogenesis are always:
questions.explanation: Among honeybees, all bees derived through parthenogenesis are males — the drones of the colony.

questions.question: Asexual reproduction is absent in which group of animals?
questions.explanation: Asexual reproduction is absent among vertebrates.
